The lowest common ancestor of these interactions is the class of compounds known as monocarboxylic acid amides, which includes both Disopyramide and Procainamide. This suggests a broader functional relationship within the antiarrhythmic agent class. The evidence supports a possible indirect pathway where Disopyramide, through its interaction with Procainamide, may influence Slc22a2, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it relies on inferred interactions and shared ancestry, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct relationship between Disopyramide and Slc22a2.
